subject.title: feat(line): per-user in-flight guard for concurrent message errors

question: Should LINE default same-user rapid follow-up events be skipped with a busy reply, or should OpenClaw preserve those follow-up messages through queueing or another active-turn feedback path?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes user-visible message delivery semantics, and tests/live proof cannot decide whether dropping a distinct second LINE message is acceptable product behavior.

options.title: Accept busy-skip after repair
options.body: Merge this shape after moving the guard before media/context work because it gives immediate feedback and avoids same-user concurrent dispatch inside the LINE plugin.

options.title: Preserve follow-up messages
options.body: Pause this branch and design a queue or active-turn feedback path so the second user message is not dropped.

options.title: Narrow the default scope
options.body: Limit the guard to the smallest accepted LINE surface, such as direct stable-sender messages, until group and postback semantics are explicitly accepted.

recommendation.title: Accept busy-skip after repair
recommendation.body: Merge this shape after moving the guard before media/context work because it gives immediate feedback and avoids same-user concurrent dispatch inside the LINE plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the strongest recent history signal across LINE handler, inbound context, media, and channel policy refactors touched by this decision.
